comment: The new-runtime gap table (#2256). This file is the only copy: #2256 links here. Each row is a gap between OpenTofu's new runtime (internal/engine) and what choudoufu needs, how it is handled while TOFU_X_EXPERIMENTAL_RUNTIME is on, and what closes it. check is one of: live (G's refusal, #2339), preflight (refused on the configuration or state before planning), post_plan (refused on the plan before it is shown or saved), engine (a diagnostic raised inside planning), accepted (not refused; named in the toggle's warning), none. Since #2397 a run that a preflight, post_plan or engine row refuses falls back to the default runtime as a whole, with a warning naming the rows, and CHOUDOUFU_NEW_RUNTIME_STRICT=1 refuses it instead, as an interim's "refuse" says; the experimental-runtime lane sets it. Preflight and post-plan rows also run on apply PLANFILE with the toggle on. A row filled by a fork port (#2376) names its package in fork_port and the switch that turns it off in switch, and its upstream list is what expires the port; internal/engine/forkport registers the port with the same rows and issues, and CHOUDOUFU_NEW_RUNTIME_NO_FORK_PORTS=1 turns every port off. Upstream issues and PRs are written as `#NNNN` and are opentofu/opentofu's.

rows.gap: any live mode on the new runtime
rows.interim: refused where NewRuntimeEnabled() is checked (TOFU_X_EXPERIMENTAL_RUNTIME_NEXT, #2339); the check where the runtime is chosen (any ConfigValueAdjuster set) was lifted by U6 (#2342), so live mode runs on the new runtime under TOFU_X_EXPERIMENTAL_RUNTIME
rows.closed_by: U6 (#2342) lifted the first check; the second stays until upstream calls _NEXT stable

rows.interim: none needed: ported by U4 (#2340)

rows.gap: markers and records at apply time
rows.interim: none needed: ported by U5 (#2341)
none needed: ported by U6 (#2342); the resolver's target becomes an import statement in the planning engine

rows.gap: markers on the create half of a replace
rows.interim: none needed: U7 (#2343) ported it; the create half of a replace is planned and final-planned through the create entry point in both orderings, and live mode no longer refuses a replace

rows.gap: cycle on a replace with newly enabled create_before_destroy
rows.interim: a fork port (#2380), not upstream's code: planning refuses an execution graph with a cycle, naming the operations in it, so a plan cannot half-apply, and the planning and apply engines record create_before_destroy in state. A replace is then not refused. The new runtime plans the upstream issue's repro without a cycle. When upstream's fix lands, the port's package, its call sites and this row's fork_port and switch are removed. With the switch set the port is off and replace actions outside live mode are refused again. Live mode does not refuse a replace since U7 (#2343)

rows.gap: destroy -target deleting what the target depends on
rows.interim: refuse a destroy plan with -target that deletes a managed object other than a target or something the prior state records as depending on one, transitively (#2387). The default runtime deletes only those; the new runtime also deletes what a target depends on (TestApply_targetedDestroy, subtest "Targeted Destroy"). A targeted destroy that deletes only the targets and their dependents is admitted
ported by U8 (#2344): the new runtime's planning engine writes the configured destroy-time arguments into the delete's prior state, and its apply engine sends them from the plan

a fork port (#2414), upstream's own pull request `#4740` cherry-picked and adapted: a data block whose configuration is wholly known and derives from no pending change is read during the plan and kept in the refreshed state; otherwise a Read change defers it to the apply, which reads it once what it depends on is applied. Pending changes are found from the values themselves (a value a planned change will alter, and a module's depends_on), and a data block with a precondition or postcondition also waits for any change pending on a managed resource it depends on, as in the default runtime. A refresh-only plan, and a destroy plan's refresh, never defer: an unreadable block keeps its prior state value, and a destroy keeps what its refresh read for the apply to evaluate and removes data sources from the final state. A data block inside a check block is read during the plan and again during the apply, and its errors are warnings. The terraform_estate_outputs blocks the in-run-estates port covers stay that port's. Data sources carry no ownership marker and no record in live mode, as on the default runtime. With the switch set the port is off and data blocks are refused again
rows.closed_by: removed, package and call sites and this row's fork_port and switch, when upstream's data-resource support lands

rows.gap: in-run estates and the terraform_estate_outputs data source
rows.interim: a fork port (#2370), not upstream's code: a data "terraform_estate_outputs" block of the builtin terraform provider plans on the new runtime. One naming an estate the run applies as a module is answered from that module's outputs and deferred to the apply while the module has changes pending; any other is read from the record store during the plan. Every other data block is the datasources fork port's (#2414) while that is on. With the switch set the port is off and the data-sources row refuses these blocks again
rows.closed_by: removed, package and call sites and this row, when upstream's data-resource support lands

rows.interim: a fork port (#2409): the planning engine forgets an orphaned or deposed object a removed block with destroy = false covers, instead of deleting it, including at the end of a moved chain, and raises the default runtime's error for a removed block whose resource or module block still exists. A removed block with destroy = true and provisioners is still refused: the default runtime runs them as destroy-time provisioners. In live mode a forget is the default runtime's: the record is deleted in the final write-back pass and the ownership marker stays on the object. With the switch set the port is off and removed blocks are refused again

rows.gap: moved blocks (not yet treated as active)
rows.interim: none needed: verified for #2378 that upstream's new runtime executes moved blocks (internal/engine/planning/plan_moved.go), including the old runtime's "Moved resource instances excluded by targeting" error under -target and -exclude; the old runtime's moved tests pass on it. A moved block next to a removed block is planned by the forget fork port (#2409), under the removed row. Live mode resolves moved blocks by marker instead: see moved-live
rows.closed_by: #2378, verified, no fork port; upstream's moved and removed work stays tracked

rows.gap: moved blocks in live mode that an ownership marker cannot follow
rows.interim: U10 (#2374): live mode resolves a moved block by marker before the engine runs. Discovery binds the object still carrying the old tofu-address to the new address, the projected prior state already holds it there, and the move finishes as an in-place tag update, so the engine never executes a move and ignores the statement, whose old address has no state entry. That holds for the shapes internal/live/moved's Honourable admits, which are the ones internal/live/lint admits and discovery aliases; every other moved block is refused here, as lint refuses it on either runtime
rows.closed_by: a moved block whose endpoints an ownership marker can follow, or choudoufu live-mv, which rewrites the marker directly

rows.interim: a fork port (#2379): upstream compiles and checks validation blocks, but refuses a condition derived from a sensitive value; the port discards a condition result's sensitive and ephemeral marks, as the old runtime does. With the switch set the port is off and validation blocks are refused again
rows.closed_by: removed, package and call site and this row's fork_port, when the new runtime accepts a condition derived from a sensitive value; upstream, not yet filed separately

rows.gap: upgrade of orphaned or deposed objects
rows.interim: none needed: verified for #2378 that upstream's new runtime upgrades, refreshes and deletes deposed objects (internal/engine/planning/plan_managed.go, planUnwantedManagedResourceInstanceObject; apply's ManagedDeposedMeta and ManagedAlreadyDeposed); the old runtime's deposed tests pass on it. lifecycle destroy = false recorded on a deposed object is forgotten by the forget fork port (#2409), under the lifecycle-destroy row

a fork port (#2381), not upstream's code: Context.Stop (Ctrl-C) asks every provider and provisioner the run opened to stop, as the default runtime's watchStop does, and a stopped plan or apply fails with "execution halted", as the default runtime's stop hook makes it. Once stopped, the apply engine starts no further managed resource apply (a create_before_destroy replace stopped after its create keeps the deposed object, as the default runtime does); a provider call already running is asked to stop and is expected to refuse or finish quickly, and other operations (final plans, data reads) are not checked. With the switch set the port is off and a stop reaches neither the providers nor the run's result
rows.closed_by: removed, package and call sites and this row, when upstream ties its engine to the run's stop

rows.warning: state after a failed or partial apply may differ from the default runtime's
behaviours upstream's own tests still skip without a category (TestContext2Apply_inconsistentWithPlan, TestContext2Apply_multiProviderDestroy and others)

rows.interim: a fork port (#2409): lifecycle { destroy = false } is recorded on the object in state, an orphaned or deposed object it or its state covers is forgotten instead of deleted (a count or for_each reduction, enabled = false, a destroy plan), a replace becomes ForgetThenCreate, and a destroy that forgot objects fails with the default runtime's error unless -suppress-forget-errors is set. With the switch set the port is off and the argument, and an object whose state records it, are refused again

a fork port (#2409), not upstream's code: check blocks and resource preconditions and postconditions are evaluated inside the new runtime's evaluator, with the default runtime's diagnostics. A resource's preconditions guard its configuration, so a failing one stops it from being planned or applied; its postconditions are checked against the planned and then the applied result, so an apply-time failure is reported after the object is saved; a check block's assertions are checked at the end of a plan and of an apply, and a failure is a warning. A resource condition failure is a warning in a refresh-only plan and is not reported by a destroy plan's refresh or by validate, as in the default runtime. Output preconditions are upstream's, and with the port on they are reported the same way and not checked in a destroy. Every check's result is recorded in the plan's checks and the state's check_results (C3, #2410), per object and per instance, with an object in a module that has no instances recorded with none, so plan JSON, show and tofu test see them as on the default runtime; a check block's scoped data source is the datasources port's (#2414). With the switch set the port is off and these blocks are refused again
rows.closed_by: removed, package and call sites and this row's fork_port and switch, when upstream's checks and conditions land

rows.interim: a fork port (#2410): upstream's evaluator marks sensitive variables, outputs and sensitive() results, but drops the marks where a value leaves evaluation; the port marks a planned change's prior and planned values (the configuration's sensitive paths, outside ignore_changes, and the schema's sensitive attributes), plans a change of sensitivity alone as an update, stores a root output unmarked with its sensitive flag, and refuses a root output whose value is sensitive but not declared sensitive, as the old runtime does. With the switch set the port is off and sensitive = true variables and outputs and the sensitive() function are refused again. An applied object is stored with its sensitive paths (the planned value's and the schema's) by an unconditional fork fix in internal/engine/applying, not by the port, so a schema-sensitive attribute reaches state and live-mode records as sensitive with the switch set too
rows.warning: with the sensitive fork port switched off, a planned change does not show attributes a provider schema marks sensitive as sensitive
rows.closed_by: removed, package and call sites and this row's fork_port, when upstream #4360 lands

rows.interim: error on any deferral not caused by -target or -exclude; plans have no record of deferral, so a post-plan check cannot see one. The deferral fork port (#2382) marks what -target or -exclude deferred with a mark of its own, so a resource whose configuration is derived only from such a result is left out of the plan as the old runtime leaves it, and gives an unknown count or for_each the old runtime's "Invalid count argument" or "Invalid for_each argument" error. Every other deferral is still refused. With the switch set the port is off and this row refuses those deferrals again
the test command runs on the default runtime with the fallback warning, since its harness still evaluates there (#2397); with CHOUDOUFU_NEW_RUNTIME_STRICT=1 it is refused
a missing input fails loudly

rows.closed_by: upstream #4768; see #2336 for the taint decision

none needed: ours, already carried

rows.gap: a plan saved on the default runtime, applied with the toggle on
rows.interim: apply follows the plan (#2397): a plan with resource changes and no execution graph was made by the default runtime and is applied there, with a warning; one with an execution graph is applied on the new runtime. Upstream's apply engine applies only plans its own planner made, so with CHOUDOUFU_NEW_RUNTIME_STRICT=1 apply still refuses the first kind with "Saved plan contains no execution graph"
rows.closed_by: #2397 (apply follows the plan); upstream for the strict refusal

rows.gap: the default runtime's per-resource tracing spans
rows.interim: a fork port (#2381), not upstream's code: plan and apply each open the default runtime's Graph walk span, and under it a plan or apply span per managed resource instance, from the engine's tracer callbacks, with the span budget and aggregate summaries of #1898. With the switch set the port is off and traces carry none of these spans
rows.closed_by: removed, package and call sites and this row, when upstream's own tracing in internal/engine lands
